questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to learn Spanish and at the same time I saw an exchange semester as an opportunity to try to live in a country that was significantly different from Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have had a fantastic experience, however, the way of being a student at a Mexican university is very different from what I know from home. I found it to be less challenging, more led by professors and less characterized by self-study, which can of course be both an advantage and a disadvantage, however I prefer the "danish" way.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it very hard to find information about the courses, which was stressfull to me when planning. However I know now that I was able to change courses during the first week of classes and therefore I wouldn't have had to stress about it :-)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Tania, the exchange coordinator from UDLAP was waiting for me at the airport in order to make sure that I was able to find the bus and arrive safely to Puebla. I also visited her office several times for help with my visa, where the university prolonged my visa (it was only valid for 3 months and I needed 6) and furthermore the international office at UDLAP helped with changing courses etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Especially super helpful that they fixed my visa problems and were waiting at the airport to help.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had a recommendation from a friend of mine who went on exchange the year before me. I was really happy to stay at my house since I lived with both Mexicans and other exchange students. The place is called Casa Leyenda / Housing Cholula and the location was perfect! The rent is super cheap and each room has their own bathroom.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
When looking for housing, the companies "Cholula Capital" and "Travels life" pop up as the first places. They are big companies that arrange trips and parties and also offer housing, hence the only people living there are exchange students. I preferred to stay at a place where there was less of a party vibe, since it is always possible to go to the parties and join the trips. 
The housing with these companies are often more expensive, and the crowd is younger (18-22). I myself was 26 when I went on exchange and therefore I was really happy with my house, where people were older and more chill and more diversified.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought it was hard finding information about courses, however I figured it all out once I was there. It seems very difficult when you are home in Denmark, but in Mexico things are easier when you just show up to an office and ask for help, dont expect to get all you answers through email... :-)

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: preregistration and then a possibility to change courses during the first week of classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Going to the international office at the university or writing them an email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Almost got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: if you want to learn or improve your Spanish, I really recommend taking the spanish test in order to be able to take classes in spanish, I took some beginner level classes and I learned a lot!!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didnt find my classes super challenging. It was a nice "break" from back home and allowed me to go on a lot of trips and explore the amazing country of Mexico.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found it easy to follow along the courses even though I took classes that differed from what I am used to back home. Not all my classes were challenging, but I still enjoyed them.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Grades are given depending on assignments during the semester, final exams, participation and attendance. In that way it is very different from back home. I found it weird that the professor took attendance, since I am used to being at university because I want to learn, however it wasn't a problem , but reminded me a little of going to gymnasium instead of uni.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Cultura Mexicana (in Spanish)
Sociolingustics 
Artistic investigation
History of International Relations
Social and Political Theory II

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really recommend taking the course Cultura Mexicana (in Spanish) and also the other spanish beginner course called Lengua y Communication. I only enrolled in the first mentioned since I thought my level was too low (I had practiced some Duolingo and could order a coffee and that was almost it), but I regretted not taking both because I really learned a lot and would have loved to have both.
I really enjoyed the teaching by -NAME REDACTED- (who taught History of International Relations). His methods are more similar to how my professors at UCPH teach and I found him very inspiring.
Sociolingustics was interesting if you want to learn more about languages and how they interact/are in contact, it was a very chill class but I enjoyed it a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Busses are a little expensive compared to how cheap traveling in general is in Mexico, however they are really comfortable and safe and a great way to experience the country

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the facilities at UDLAP are great! The campus is very well kept with green gardens and water fountains. There is free access to tennis courts, outdoor swimming pool, gym etc at campus! remember to bring your own gear or buy something when arriving

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of events arranged such as Mexican folk dancing, celebrations of "dia de muertos" and other national holidays and also football matches etc. Make sure to join them! the university uses many funds on this and it is a great way to experience Mexican culture.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go watch Mexican folk dancing, celebrations of "dia de muertos" and other events at the big auditorium. You get an email when there is something coming up, some are free and others cost around 30 dkk-100 dkk.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take as many trips as possible. I made sure to have Fridays off from classes and in that way I was able to go away for more than just two days.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it extremely hard in the first two days / half week. Everything seems so different than Denmark: the sounds, the houses, the food, the language etc. I missed my friends, family and boyfriend, however it turned around quickly and I met a lot of other exchange students, that also had the same experience as me. Now, I am super happy that I fought through the hard part in the beginning.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Mexican people are some of the nicest and most welcoming people I have ever met and all the other exchange students were exited to meet new people too.
My best advice is to attend a lot of things with other students, arrange trips etc, but also remember to take some time off. I usually relax when I am with other people, but I experienced that being with people that I didnt know very well didnt necessarily give me more energy even though I liked spending time with them. And if you want to skip an event, it is completely okay, people rarely remember if you went to all of the parties, trips, game nights etc <33

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mexico is a very loud country! I was woken up every morning by roosters and fireworks from the nearby church. Remember to bring earplugs.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The people are extremely welcoming and warm. Everyone always greets eachother and Mexicans really want to help if you are lost or need any help.
The food is amazing too, and then I was overwhelmed by all festivities and richness of culture. Mexicans are really good at celebrating and it is amazing to experience things such as dia de muertos, Independence Day, Posadas (in Christmas time) and other things!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Learn Spanish! Not many Mexicans outside the bigger cities speak English, but they are really nice and helpful when they hear that you try to learn and speak their language.
Try to meet Mexican people, since they are extremely hospitable and welcoming. You will have so many great experiences if invited by a Mexican to something.
Pack lightly if you like vintage/second hand clothes - there are both flea markets and great second hand shops in Cholula. I bought a lot and had to carry two big suitcases home, since I had brought too much from home too.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to UDLAP and Mexico if you want to experience the country, the culture and the nature. I have learned more schoolwise at UCPH, so dont go if you only want to go to classes and afterwards sit in your room and study :-D

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning to live alone in a country very different from Denmark and experiencing the richness of Mexico and how lovely people in Mexico are.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first week, settling in a new country where you dont know the language and where everything seems different. But give it time and tell yourself it is okay to feel homesick. It is really worth it

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Take some spanish courses outside the university! it is super cheap and you learn a lot

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
